meta.question: Lab report parser should upload pdf's using anthropic's upload functionality and then sending messages instead of just sending message with b64_image of each page sequentially like it does here https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support#send-your-first-pdf-request

claims.content: Done looks like: Decision-ready brief with evidence
The Files API requires the beta header `anthropic-beta: files-api-2025-04-14` on every request, including both the upload call and the messages.create call.

Python SDK upload method: `client.beta.files.upload(file=("document.pdf", open("/path/to/document.pdf", "rb"), "application/pdf"))`. Returns an object with an `.id` field (the file_id). The client must be `anthropic.Anthropic()` and the call goes through `client.beta.files`, not `client.files`.

To reference an uploaded PDF in a messages call, use a `document` content block with `source.type = "file"` and `source.file_id = <file_id>`. The messages call must use `client.beta.messages.create(...)` (not `client.messages.create`) and must pass `betas=["files-api-2025-04-14"]`. Example source block: `{"type": "file", "file_id": "file_011CNha8iCJcU1wXNR6q4V8w"}`.

File size limit: 500 MB per file. Total org storage: 500 GB. Rate limit (beta): ~100 requests/minute for file API calls. Files persist until deleted (no automatic expiry). Files are scoped to the workspace of the API key — any key in the same workspace can use them.

Files API supports: PDF (`application/pdf` -> `document` block), plain text (`text/plain` -> `document` block), images (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif`, `image/webp` -> `image` block), and datasets/others for code execution tool (`container_upload` block). CSV, XLSX, DOCX, MD are NOT directly supported as document blocks — they must be converted to plain text first.

Files API file_id references are supported in all models that support the given file type. PDFs via file_id are supported in all Claude 3.5+ models. Files API is NOT supported on Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI — direct API only.

Native PDF support works by: (1) extracting text from each page, (2) converting each page to an image, (3) providing Claude with both the text and image of each page simultaneously as a `document` block. This is different from the current app approach of rasterizing to PNG then sending each page as a separate `image` block in serial API calls. Native PDF support uses a single `document` block per PDF regardless of page count.

PDF limits: max request payload size 32 MB (varies by platform), max 600 pages per request (100 for models with 200k-token context window). Both limits cover the entire request payload. For large PDFs, using Files API keeps payload small by referencing file_id instead of re-sending bytes. Dense PDFs (complex tables, heavy graphics) can exhaust context window before page limit.

PDFs can be sent to Claude via three source types in a `document` block: (1) `type: "url"` with a `url` field pointing to a hosted PDF, (2) `type: "base64"` with `media_type: "application/pdf"` and a `data` field containing base64-encoded bytes, (3) `type: "file"` with a `file_id` from the Files API. All three result in the same native PDF processing (text + image per page).

Current `services/lab_report_parser.py` uses PyMuPDF to rasterize each page at 200 DPI to PNG, then base64-encodes each PNG and sends them to Claude as `image` blocks one page at a time via separate `client.messages.create` calls with `type: "base64", media_type: "image/png"`. It does NOT use the native `document` block or the Files API at all.
The Files API is in beta and is NOT eligible for Zero Data Retention (ZDR). Beta features are excluded from ZDR. This is a compliance constraint for customers with ZDR requirements.

File API operations (upload, download, list, metadata, delete) are free. File content used in Messages requests is priced as normal input tokens. Uploaded PDFs processed as `document` blocks cost both text tokens (~1,500–3,000 tokens/page) and image tokens (per-page image cost). The image token cost is the same as the current approach, but text extraction tokens are additive.

To migrate the parser to use the Files API: (1) Remove PyMuPDF rasterization entirely, (2) Upload the raw PDF bytes once via `client.beta.files.upload(file=("report.pdf", pdf_bytes_io, "application/pdf"))`, (3) Replace the per-page `_extract_from_page` loop with a single `client.beta.messages.create(..., betas=["files-api-2025-04-14"], messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "document", "source": {"type": "file", "file_id": file_id}}, {"type": "text", ...}]}])`, (4) Optionally delete the file after the call or retain for caching. The `document` block supports optional `title`, `context`, and `citations` fields.

The Files API is still in beta (header `files-api-2025-04-14`). Beta APIs can change or have breaking changes before GA. The rate limit during beta is ~100 requests/minute for file operations, which could become a bottleneck for batch processing workloads.

The `document` content block (for both base64 and file sources) supports optional fields: `title` (string), `context` (string describing the document), and `citations` (`{"enabled": true}`). These are not required for basic extraction but `citations` can improve accuracy when enabled.

Confirmed via official docs: sending a file_id in a messages call requires `client.beta.messages.create(...)` with `betas=["files-api-2025-04-14"]`. The standard `client.messages.create` does NOT support the `file` source type. The `client.beta` path is required specifically because the Files API is a beta feature — it is NOT an optional convention.

source.artifact: Files API docs — 'Using a file in messages' section

claims.content: The distinction between client.messages.create and client.beta.messages.create depends on what source type is used: (1) Sending a PDF as `type: "base64"` in a document block uses `client.messages.create` — no beta needed. (2) Sending a PDF via `type: "file"` with a file_id from the Files API requires `client.beta.messages.create` + `betas=["files-api-2025-04-14"]`. The beta path is only required when referencing an uploaded file_id.

Dry-run confirmed: parser_files_api.py imports cleanly, Pydantic models are reused unchanged, no new package dependencies are introduced. The new implementation is a valid drop-in replacement for extract_from_pdf at the structural level.

Measured on a 1-page synthetic COA PDF (1,466 bytes): the current approach rasterizes to a 147,849-byte PNG then base64-encodes to 197,132 bytes sent in the message body. The Files API approach sends only ~200 bytes (the file_id) in the message body — a 99% reduction per page. For a 3-page COA, old = ~591 KB in message bodies; new = ~200 bytes.

Migration removes 3 functions (rasterize_pdf ~25 lines, _extract_from_page ~35 lines, _merge_extractions ~30 lines) and the `import fitz` line. Adds `import io` (stdlib) and wraps the entire pipeline in a single extract_from_pdf function of ~30 lines. Net: ~90 lines removed, 0 new dependencies.

For a 1-page COA: old = 1 messages.create call; new = 3 calls (upload + messages + delete). For a 3-page COA: old = 3 calls; new = 3 calls (equal). For N>3 pages: new wins on call count. For all page counts: new wins on per-call payload size (200 bytes vs 197 KB/page). The new approach is never worse on total bytes transferred.

Live run on a 1-page synthetic COA: both approaches extracted identical results — 10 terpenes, 8 cannabinoids, confidence=5, total_terpenes=1.561, lab_name='Green Leaf Analytics LLC', pass_fail='PASS'. Extraction quality is at parity for a clean text-layer PDF.

Live run on a 1-page synthetic COA: old approach 5.08s, new approach 6.01s (+0.93s). The new approach is slower on 1-page PDFs due to 2 extra calls (upload + delete). NOTE: original projection that 'latency shifts for N>1 pages' was refuted by x001 — see x001 for corrected multi-page analysis.

Tested on a 3-page synthetic COA: the old parser made exactly 1 API call (early exit fired at line 342 of lab_report_parser.py: `if result.terpenes and result.cannabinoids and result.confidence >= 3: break`). Old elapsed: 4.72s. New elapsed: 6.86s. Old was still faster by 2.15s on a 3-page PDF. p006's claim that 'latency advantage shifts toward new for N>1' is false for typical well-formatted COAs — early exit means old stays at 1 call regardless of page count as long as page 1 yields confidence≥3 with terpenes+cannabinoids.

The latency crossover (where new approach becomes faster) only occurs when old approach processes 2+ pages — i.e. when page 1 yields: no terpenes, OR no cannabinoids, OR confidence < 3. This is the exception (bad/unusual COA), not the norm. For all typical well-formatted COAs the old approach remains faster due to early exit keeping it at 1 message call (~5s) vs new always at 3 calls (~6s).

CheckWeedNY API dataset (as of 2026-04-12): 32,518 total COAs, 671 unique clients (dispensaries/processors), 532 unique brands, 26 unique labs. Dataset spans tests from 2008 through April 2026. Average THC across all records: 37.4%.
CheckWeedNY API authenticates via `X-API-Key` request header. Base URL: `https://api.checkweedny.com/v1`. No OAuth or session tokens needed. Key format observed: `cwny_live_<hex>`.

GET /v1/coas returns `{data: [...], total: N}`. Each record includes: `id` (string, e.g. `buddega-23236`), `brand_name`, `product_name`, `product_type`, `normalized_product_type`, `batch_number`, `lab_name`, `test_date`, `license_number`, `client_name`, `pdf_url` (direct link to source PDF), `parse_confidence` (0.0–1.0), `is_duplicate` (int), `total_terpenes_pct`, `dominant_terpene`, `terpene_count`, plus inline cannabinoid fields: `d9_thc_pct`, `thca_pct`, `total_thc_pct`, `cbd_pct`, `cbda_pct`, `total_cbd_pct`, `cbg_pct`, `cbn_pct`, `cbc_pct`, `thcv_pct`, `d8_thc_pct`, `total_cannabinoids_pct`, and pass/fail booleans for metals, microbials, mycotoxins, pesticides, solvents.

GET /v1/coas/:id returns the full list schema PLUS nested arrays: `terpenes: [{compound, value_pct}]`, `pesticides: [{compound, result_ppm, loq_ppm, action_limit_ppm, pass}]`, `solvents: [{compound, result_ppm, loq_ppm, action_limit_ppm, pass}]`, `heavy_metals: {arsenic_ug_g, cadmium_ug_g, lead_ug_g, mercury_ug_g, chromium_ug_g, nickel_ug_g, copper_ug_g, antimony_ug_g, overall_pass}`, `microbials: {total_aerobic_bacteria_cfu_g, total_yeast_mold_cfu_g, e_coli_detected, salmonella_detected, aspergillus_*_detected, overall_microbial_pass}`, `mycotoxins: {aflatoxin_b1_ppm, aflatoxin_b2_ppm, ..., ochratoxin_a_ppm, overall_pass}`. Individual terpene compound data is ONLY available in the detail endpoint, not the list.

Terpene data is sparse: in the Ayrloom brand sample (393 COAs), all 5 sampled records had `total_terpenes_pct: null` and `terpene_count: null`. Flower/concentrate COAs from other brands (e.g. Fernway/Tyson 2.0) do have terpene data (3.95% total, 12–13 compounds). Terpenes are absent for most ingestibles, tinctures, and topicals. The `terpene_count` field in the list response is a reliable null-check before fetching the detail endpoint.

SUPERSEDED BY x003. Original test used wrong param names (field names instead of short names). `brand`, `batch_number`, `license_number`, `product_name` all returned full dataset — but these are not the correct param names. See x003 for correct filter params.

Every COA record includes a `pdf_url` field pointing to the source PDF (hosted by the originating retailer/processor). This URL can be used to fetch the actual COA PDF for downstream processing (e.g. passing to the existing Claude PDF parser). Some URLs are alleaves.com CDN links; others are direct processor-hosted URLs (e.g. fernway.com/wp-content/).

`parse_confidence` field (0.0–1.0) reflects how well CheckWeedNY's own parser extracted data from the source PDF. Observed range: 0.5 (garbled product name, low quality), 0.7 (good — most Ayrloom records), ~1.0 (excellent — Fernway/Smithers CTS records). Can be used as a pre-filter: records with confidence < 0.7 should fall back to Claude parsing.

Integration strategy: use CheckWeedNY as a 'try first' lookup before running Claude PDF parsing. Flow: (1) search by brand (required) + paginate through results to match by batch_number client-side [CONTRADICTED by x004 — use ?batch= directly], (2) if found with parse_confidence >= 0.7 AND terpene_count > 0, map API fields directly to COAExtraction model — skip Claude entirely, (3) if found but terpene_count is null (common for non-flower), fetch pdf_url and run through Claude PDF parser, (4) if not found, fall back to existing upload+parse flow. This can eliminate Claude calls for a significant share of well-documented flower/concentrate products.

Risk (PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED by x003): `brand` is NOT the only filter — `?batch=`, `?license=`, `?product=` also work with correct short param names. Residual risk: exact-match semantics are unknown for `?product=` (may be substring). `?brand=` exact-match sensitivity is also unconfirmed. If brand/batch values in our DB use different casing or formatting than CheckWeedNY's values, lookup will silently return wrong results.

Risk: terpenes are null for most ingestibles, tinctures, topicals, and beverages in the CheckWeedNY dataset. The terpenomics app is terpene-focused. For the product categories most likely to lack terpene data, CheckWeedNY lookup would always fall through to Claude PDF parsing — providing no benefit for those SKUs. The value proposition is highest for flower and concentrate products.

CONTRADICTS r023: The API DOES support batch, license, and product server-side filters — but uses short param names, not the field names tested in r023. Confirmed working: `?batch=<batch_number>` (total: 1 for exact match), `?license=<license_number>` (total: 214 for OCM-PROC-24-000068), `?product=Gelato` (total: 685). NOT working: `?batch_number=`, `?license_number=`, `?product_name=`, `?name=`, `?client=`, `?client_id=`, `?q=`, `?search=`. Pattern: API uses abbreviated param names. This substantially changes the integration strategy — batch-level exact lookup is possible without client-side scanning.

CONTRADICTS r026 step (1): r026 says 'search by brand (required) + paginate through results to match by batch_number client-side'. This is wrong — x003 confirmed `?batch=<batch_number>` returns exactly 1 result directly. No brand filter needed, no client-side scanning. The correct primary lookup is `GET /v1/coas?batch=<batch_number>`, and brand can be omitted entirely. This removes an entire step from the integration flow.

r026's parse_confidence >= 0.7 threshold has a 28% miss rate in the flower category (14/50 sampled COAs had confidence < 0.7; values seen: 0.3, 0.5, 0.6). These records would fall back to Claude parsing even though they exist in the dataset. This is not a contradiction of r026 (the threshold still works as a quality gate) but the 28% figure is evidence that the threshold significantly constrains hit rate for the most terpene-rich category.

~2% of COAs in the dataset have null `batch_number`. r026 relies on batch_number as the lookup key, but these records cannot be found by `?batch=` at all. For products where our DB has a batch number but the COA has none, the lookup silently returns 0 results and falls back to Claude — which is acceptable. For products where our DB has no batch number, no lookup is possible at all via any confirmed filter.

Terpene compound names in the API use a specific capitalization/format: 'Alpha-Pinene', 'Beta-Pinene', 'Caryophyllene Oxide', 'Bisabolol', 'Fenchol', 'Sabinene', 'Borneol', 'Nerol'. Claude may return different variants (e.g. 'β-Caryophyllene', 'β-Pinene', 'trans-Nerolidol'). COAExtraction.name is unconstrained (plain str), so no validation errors occur, but inconsistent names between API-sourced and Claude-sourced records will break any downstream terpene aggregation or deduplication that relies on name equality.

Confirmed working /v1/coas filter params (live-tested 2026-04-12): `brand` (partial, case-insensitive — 'ayrl'/'AYRLOOM'/'Ayrloom' all return same 393 results), `lab` (partial, case-insensitive), `product` (partial, case-insensitive), `batch` (partial, case-insensitive — full batch string returns 0–1 results in practice), `license` (exact match), `matrix` (Title Case values: 'Flower'=15420, 'Edible'=6054, 'Concentrate'; docs incorrectly state lowercase), `min_thc`, `max_thc` (numeric range filters, both working), `sort` ('test_date'|'total_thc_pct'|'brand_name'), `order` ('asc'|'desc'), `page` (1-indexed), `limit` (1–100). NOT working: `since`, `until` (both return full 32,518-record set — date range filtering is broken in the current API).

Prototype sync.py implements a two-step lookup: (1) ?batch=<batch_id> via linked LabReport (exact, 1 result), (2) ?brand=<brand>&product=<name> substring fallback. Only writes when parse_confidence >= 0.7 and terpene_count > 0. Mirrors _apply_terpenes_to_product upsert pattern from lab_reports.py.

Prototype includes a 30-entry normalization map converting CheckWeedNY compound names to our canonical terpene names (e.g. "Caryophyllene" -> "β-Caryophyllene", "Alpha-Pinene" -> "α-Pinene"). Unmapped names pass through as-is, which risks silent duplicates in product_terpenes if the same compound appears under two names across API-sourced and Claude-sourced records.

Sync script supports --dry-run (default), --write, --skip-existing, --product-id, --brand, and --min-confidence flags. Output statuses: written, dry_run, skipped, not_found, low_confidence, no_terpenes, error. Batch lookup requires a linked LabReport with batch_id — products without lab reports can only be found by brand+name substring match.

CHALLENGES brief recommendation to insert CheckWeedNY lookup into the upload/process flow: batch_id — the primary lookup key per x004 — is extracted by Claude at lab_reports.py:225 (report.batch_id = extraction.batch_id). It does not exist before extract_from_pdf() runs. The ?batch= lookup therefore cannot precede Claude in the upload flow; it is only usable after a prior parse has already populated LabReport.batch_id.

CHALLENGES brief recommendation to insert CheckWeedNY lookup into the upload/process flow: product_id is optional in ProcessRequest (lab_reports.py:173) and often absent when the admin is processing a newly uploaded PDF. Without product_id, there is no brand or product_name to query ?brand=&product= with. Even when product_id is provided, adding a remote API call to a user-facing endpoint creates a new failure mode: CheckWeedNY downtime or rate limiting would surface as 502 errors on what should be a reliable admin action.

CheckWeedNY enrichment belongs in the bulk sync script (prototypes/checkweedny-bulk-sync/sync.py), NOT the upload/process flow. Reasons: (1) batch_id is unavailable before parsing (x008), (2) product_id is often absent at process time (x009), (3) the admin uploading a PDF already has the document and intends it to be parsed — a pre-parse lookup adds latency with no benefit, (4) the bulk sync script runs asynchronously, can be retried on failure, and targets the entire product catalog rather than coupling enrichment to individual upload events. Recommended separation of concerns: upload/process = parse PDFs the admin deliberately submitted; sync script = proactively enrich all products from the API.
